scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Internet traffic from all internal users became slower and
sometimes flaky. Active TCP connections kept working but new
connections to 203.0.113.x sometimes time out then succeed.
R1 reports it lost an OSPF neighbor. Identify which.

injection.action: kill ospfd on ISPA (primary internet default-originator)

pre_check.command: vtysh -c "show ip ospf neighbor" | grep -c Full

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: ispa ospfd daemon
Mechanism: Both ISPA and ISPB advertise a default route into
  the OSPF domain via `default-information originate`. R1
  prefers ISPA (lower cost). When ISPA's ospfd dies, R1
  ages out the default learned from ISPA and falls back to
  ISPB's default. During the timeout + reconvergence window,
  new connections fail. Once converged on ISPB, service
  resumes but takes a slightly different path.
Localization: ispa
Root cause: ospfd not running on ispa
Fix: `/etc/init.d/frr restart` on ispa

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is missing/empty on ispa" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: OSPF adjacencies between R1 and the core switches, carried over interfaces that are members of Linux bridges on csw1/csw2. The bridged core interconnect (bond0 on csw1/csw2) also flapped.

Mechanism: The core peer link aggregation changed (bond0 speed jumped 10G->20G), triggering STP topology changes. During reconvergence, forwarding on the bridged ports briefly stopped, so OSPF hellos from R1 were missed and its neighbor adjacencies expired and reformed. Existing TCP flows survived via the remaining path, but new connections to 203.0.113.x intermittently failed while routing reconverged.

Localization: On R1, both OSPF neighbors currently show short uptimes (~1 minute): 10.0.0.77 on eth0 (csw1) and 10.0.0.78 on eth1 (csw2) [r1 “show ip ospf neighbor”]. On csw1 and csw2, FRR logs record OSPF DD negotiation with R1 at 23:51:18, confirming recent adjacency resets with neighbor 10.0.0.76 (R1) [csw1/csw2 /var/log/frr/frr.log]. Both csw1 and csw2 kernels report repeated “br0: topology change detected” messages around the same time, and zebra reports “bond0 old speed: 10000 new speed: 20000,” indicating bond membership change and STP TCNs.

Root cause: A bonding/L2 change on the csw1/csw2 core peer (bond0) caused STP reconvergence that temporarily blocked OSPF on the bridged WAN-facing ports, making R1 lose its OSPF neighbors with csw1 (RID 10.0.0.77, eth0) and csw2 (RID 10.0.0.78, eth1).

Corrective fix: Remove WAN/R1-facing interfaces from the Linux bridge or enable “edge/portfast” behavior to prevent STP impact on routed links; stabilize the bond (consistent LACP settings) to avoid flaps; alternatively, run OSPF on unbridged routed interfaces or a dedicated VRF/VLAN so STP events cannot interrupt routing adjacencies.

per_axis.rationale: The submission never identifies ispa; it blames csw1/csw2 bond/STP events and OSPF adjacencies on R1 instead of ospfd on ispa.
The writeup explicitly diagnoses OSPF/ospf adjacencies and cites OSPF-specific logs and neighbors, so the OSPF component is clearly identified.
The report never mentions ISPA/ISPB default advertisement or R1 switching to ISPB's default route, so it fails to explain the ISPB failover.
The writeup recommends removing interfaces from the bridge/using portfast or stabilizing the bond rather than performing the expected action (/etc/init.d/frr restart on ispa).

The agent's writeup asserts a bond/STP-induced OSPF flap on the core switches, but the investigation log contains a direct observation that ospfd is not running on ispa which the writeup ignores; claims about bond speed changes, STP TCNs, or zebra messages are not supported by the provided logs.
